bill.title: Medicare Hearing Aid Coverage Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
bill.officialSummary: Medicare Hearing Aid Coverage Act of 2025 This bill allows for Medicare coverage of hearing aids and related examinations. The Government Accountability Office must study programs that provide assistance for hearing aids and related examinations for individuals with hearing loss.

classification.plainSummary: This bill would expand Medicare to cover hearing aids and the examinations needed to fit them. Currently, Medicare does not pay for hearing aids. The bill also directs the Government Accountability Office to study existing programs that help people with hearing loss obtain hearing aids and related services.

industries.rationale: Medical device manufacturers that produce hearing aids would gain a new Medicare reimbursement market.
Audiologists and other providers conducting hearing examinations would receive Medicare payment for services currently not covered.
Medicare Advantage plans and supplemental insurers would face new coverage obligations and cost structures for hearing aids.

plain.whatItDoes: This bill would allow for Medicare coverage of hearing aids and related examinations.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in what Medicare pays for. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
